# Commands

```text
instagram-archiver [options] {login,profile,relayout,fill-videos,scan,followers,post} ...
```

Every command accepts the [common options](options.qmd). The ones listed below
are extra.

---

## `login`

Open a window and wait for manual login.

```bash
instagram-archiver login
```

Log in yourself, two-factor included. The session is saved to a per-user
browser profile directory and reused by every later run, so you do this once
per account. Override the location with `--browser-profile`.

---

## `profile`

Archive every visible post on a profile.

```bash
instagram-archiver profile https://www.instagram.com/someaccount/
```

| Extra option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--max-posts N` | stop after N posts, useful for a first test run |

Photographs are saved by default; videos need `--videos`, and a video that was
not saved leaves [a placeholder](output.qmd#placeholders). Reels are archived
too - they are ordinary posts of the account's own - unless you pass
`--skip-reels`.

---

## `post`

Archive one specific post URL.

```bash
instagram-archiver post https://www.instagram.com/p/ABC123/
```

Works with `/p/` and `/reel/` URLs.

---

## `scan`

Record what a profile posted - dates, counts, captions - **without downloading
any media**.

```bash
instagram-archiver scan https://www.instagram.com/someaccount/
```

| Extra option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--max-posts N` | stop after N posts |

One row per post in the account's `metadata/posts.csv` and `posts.json`: date
and exact timestamp, post or reel, photo and video counts, likes, comment
count, play count and caption. About **3 seconds a post**, against 30 for
archiving.

::: {.callout-note title="Play counts need the account itself"}

Instagram leaves `view_count` null in every post's page data, but draws it
on the reels tab, which the account can see about itself. `scan` reads it
there. See [what is visible](visibility.qmd#view-counts).

:::

---

## `followers`

Record who follows an account, and what changed since last time.

```bash
instagram-archiver followers https://www.instagram.com/someaccount/
```

Writes a dated snapshot of the names to `metadata/followers/` and appends a
row to `metadata/followers.csv`, then reports who joined or left since the
previous snapshot.

**Its own command, never part of archiving.** A snapshot records the count it
was aiming for and whether it matched, and two partial snapshots are never
compared - a name missing from one run is usually a name that run did not see,
not somebody who left.

::: {.callout-warning title="Complete only for accounts you can log in as"}

Read as a viewer the follower dialog is virtualised: five different
strategies each returned 432-459 of one account's 603 names. Logged in as
that account, the same code returned all 606.

:::

---

## `fill-videos`

Fetch only the videos an earlier run skipped, using the index.

```bash
instagram-archiver fill-videos
```

Reads the index, visits only the posts holding a placeholder, and ignores the
profile entirely. Filling 15 videos across 6 posts took **131 seconds**,
against about 14 minutes to walk the whole profile.

---

## `relayout`

Rearrange an archive already on disk. **No browser, no network.**

```bash
instagram-archiver relayout --nested --dry-run
instagram-archiver relayout --nested
```

| Extra option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | list what would move, without moving anything |

Nothing is re-downloaded: files move into their new place, the index is
updated, and folders left empty are tidied up. It works in both directions.
